html:
The unfree people of Laconia and Messenia, owned by the Spartan state and forced to farm the land of Spartan citizens. They outnumbered the Spartans many times over.

Most were the descendants of peoples conquered by Sparta, above all the Messenians after the First Messenian War. They could not be sold abroad or freed by a single master, since they belonged to the state. They handed over a fixed share of their harvest, which fed the Spartan men in their common messes and freed them to train full time for war.

Sparta lived in fear of them. Each year the ephors declared war on the helots, so killing one was not murder, and young Spartans in the Krypteia hunted those who seemed dangerous. Revolts came after the earthquake of 464 BCE and at other times. In 369 BCE the Theban general Epaminondas freed Messenia, and the Messenian helots became free citizens of a refounded Messene. Laconian helots remained until Roman times.
sum: The unfree people of Laconia and Messenia, owned by the Spartan state and forced to farm the land of Spartan citizens. They outnumbered the Spartans many times over.
